4.0.s.en: (1) The offering of Abel and Cain

4.0.0.en: Knew: what is meant is the bodily relationship, and this means that it is not merely a material relationship but is acquaintance, affection and love that lead to a bodily relationship.

4.0.1.en: After the sentence of death was passed on man, the bodily relationship began as an expression of love and for the begetting of offspring and the preservation of the kind. This relationship is not connected with sin but is a holy relationship that God placed in His plan when He created man, for He said to Adam and Eve after creating them, "Be fruitful, and multiply, and replenish the earth" (ch. 1:28). And when Eve conceived, she bore a son and called him Cain, because she rejoiced in the grace of God given to her, as she said, "I have gotten a man from the LORD", because God had promised that her seed would bruise the serpent's head, so Eve rejoiced at the beginning of the offspring who would crush Satan so that she would obtain salvation.

4.1.0.en: Eve conceived and bore a second son, Abel, and it is implicitly understood that she bore daughters who are not mentioned, and they are the ones whom her sons married.

4.1.1.en: Abel worked as a keeper of sheep, which gave him quiet ways and an inclination to contemplation and prayer, while Cain worked in tilling the ground, so he was rougher and more occupied with material things. Abel is a type of those who love contemplation and prayer, while Cain is a type of those occupied with the works of the world and earthly pleasures.

4.2.0.en: Cain offered some of the plants that he cultivated in the ground as an offering to God, and He did not accept it, while Abel his younger brother offered of the best of his sheep a sacrifice to God, and God was pleased with it and accepted it .. and there are differences between the two offerings:

4.2.1.en: 1- Abel obeyed the word of God that He had taught his father Adam, to draw near to Him by offering animal sacrifices and burning them, while Cain did not care and offered some crops.

4.2.2.en: 2- Abel offered of the best of his sheep (firstlings), while Cain offered some plants, not the best of them nor the firstfruits of his produce.

4.2.3.en: 3- Abel believed that this animal sacrifice was a type of the sacrifice of Christ the Redeemer in the fullness of time, as he learned from his father Adam, and as is mentioned in the Epistle to the Hebrews, "By faith Abel offered unto God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain" (Heb 11:3).

4.3.0.en: When God rejected Cain's offering, he did not examine himself to repent and correct his mistakes in what he offered to God, but was angry in pride because his offering was rejected by God while his brother's offering was accepted. His fall into sin is expressed by "his countenance fell", that is, he did not think spiritually and heavenly, but was vexed with his brother instead of benefiting from him.

4.4.0.en: When God saw Cain fallen into sin in his thought, He warned him to repent and called him to good conduct by lifting up his heart to God, because if he did not think well, sin would take control of him and turn from thought into deed. For it was still at the door of his heart, and by his will he could reject it, but if he was negligent, sin would rule over him, that is, he would fall into actual murder, because the sin of anger, if it increases, reaches murder; therefore Christ warned against anger when He mentioned His commandment, Thou shalt not kill, and commanded us not to be angry (Mt 5:21, 22).

4.4.1.en: God warns you in various ways to turn back from your sins, so do not neglect His warnings, and respond to His call to draw near to Him in prayer and to abide in His Church and her sacraments, so that Satan will not prevail against you.

4.5.0.en: Cain harbored evil against his brother Abel, so he pretended to talk normally with him and drew him out to the field, lest, if he tried to kill him at home, his parents or his sisters would stand before him. And when he found a suitable opportunity in the field, far from the eyes, he stretched out his hand and killed him, as he had seen the animals slaughtered and die. All this shows the hardness and roughness of Cain's heart.

4.6.0.en: God in His love went to Cain to call him to repentance, and asked him about his brother Abel, perhaps he would confess his sin. But he, impudently, answered God that he did not know where his brother was. By this he is a liar and even insolent toward God, blaming Him for His question by saying that he had not been charged with guarding his brother.

4.7.0.en: Since Cain refused to repent, God confronted him with his sin, that he had killed his brother, and that He does not keep silent about injustice, but that even if the wronged one has died, God demands his right, and the wrongdoer must bear his punishment for his wrong.

4.8.0.en: God pronounced His punishment on Cain by the curse, that is, the loss of blessing, and the earth he used to cultivate bears witness to his wrong to his brother, since his shed blood fell upon it, and therefore it would not give him blessing in its produce.

4.9.0.en: He added to the punishment, besides the loss of blessing, restlessness and wandering in the earth, and indeed from his restlessness he flees from place to place and never feels rest.

4.10.0.en: Cain felt the hideousness of his sin when the punishment was pronounced on him, and even declared his inability to bear this punishment, whether the loss of blessing or the restlessness leading to wandering, and he added also that he had become liable to death at the hand of whoever met him, and by these he means:

4.10.2.en: 2- Any persons in the world whom he had not seen before, since he had come to fear the unknown.

4.10.3.en: 3- The fear of the animals attacking him and killing him.

4.11.0.en: Of God's mercy to Cain was His promise that whoever killed him would be punished sevenfold, and He did not promise him that he would not be killed, perhaps so that his restlessness would lead him to repentance, but unfortunately he did not repent. On the other hand, He gave him a divine sign that protects him from death and frightens whoever tries to kill him, and some say it was the sign of the Cross or some other sign that we do not know.

4.12.0.en: Cain departed from God and was separated from Him because of his sins and dwelt in the land of "Nod", which means wandering, and thus he lived in the punishment of sin all the days of his life.

4.12.1.en: If you suffer from the results of your sins, do not complain, but return to God in repentance and be confident that He will forgive you, then rise to make up for what you have lost with a deeper relationship of love with God and love for those around you.

4.13.0.en: He confirms here that the bodily relationship, as we mentioned, is acquaintance, understanding and love.

4.13.1.en: Cain's wife was his sister, for this was permitted, since there were no women except his sisters, and they are not mentioned, but their birth is implicitly understood.

4.13.2.en: And Cain begot his first son Enoch, which means disciplined or trained, for Cain, who was far from God, tries to bring up his children in a sound upbringing, but this is not possible so long as he has departed from God, so only the name remains for him, without the deed.

4.13.3.en: And since Cain felt wandering and flight from the presence of God (v. 14) because of his sin, he needed to settle down, so instead of returning to God in repentance to regain his peace, he tried to solve his problem in a material way, so he built a city and called it after the name of his son Enoch, pretending settledness and discipline, although he had lost all this because of his insistence on staying far from God.

4.14.0.en: He mentions the descendants of Cain: Enoch begot Irad, and the meaning of his name is city, to confirm the illusory settledness that he made for himself by building a city. And Irad begot a son whom he named Mehujael, that is, smitten of God, and this confirms his sense of guilt and God's anger against him. And Mehujael begot Methusael, which means a hero from God, for his heart turned to material power and to oppressing others, and claims that this is from God. Then Methusael begot Lamech, and the meaning of his name is strong, and he means the same meaning as Methusael, that is, material power.

4.14.1.en: If you fall into any sin, hasten to repentance and do not try to cover it with justifications and pretend the opposite, for all this is like the fig leaves that Adam made for himself, which are of no avail, but keep man away from God. And would that the names of your children have meanings that benefit them spiritually.

4.15.0.en: This is another proof of absorption in material things, and it is the first mention of a man marrying two wives.

4.15.1.en: Adah means beauty and Zillah means shadow, that is, he was immersed in preoccupation with material desires and their shadows. This is a natural result of being far from God, of not repenting, and of relying on human strength and material settledness and not on God.

4.16.0.en: Adah's first son was Jabal, who worked in tending sheep, so he was a nomad dwelling in tents, and his sons followed the same trade, which is shepherding. The meaning of his name is wanderer, and it is suitable for his trade, which is shepherding.

4.17.0.en: The second son of Adah she called Jubal, and its meaning is the player of musical instruments such as the harp and the pipe, and that was his work for which he became famous.

4.18.0.en: As for the second wife, Zillah, she bore a son whom she named Tubal-cain, and its meaning is copper, and he discovered the copper found on the surface of the earth and made from it musical instruments on which he played, and it was also used in various works. Then she bore a sister of his whom she named Naamah, and its meaning is beauty or beloved, because this was their chief preoccupation, that is, material beauty.

4.19.0.en: To my wounding: my breaking, for "shadakh" means to break.

4.19.1.en: Lamech stood before his two wives boasting in pride that he was strong and able to overcome any man who stood before him, and whoever tried to wound him or break him he would kill at once, and he wrote this sentence, with the following verse, in poetry, since he was boasting and singing of his material strength. Perhaps he used the sword that his son Tubal-cain invented from copper, and therefore some commentators call these two verses the song of the sword.

4.20.0.en: Going further in his pride, he says that if God had promised to avenge sevenfold whoever killed Cain, then whoever tried to kill Lamech, God would avenge him seventy and sevenfold, although God had not promised him anything, but his pride made him think this.

4.21.0.en: When Eve bore Cain, she thought he was the seed through whom the bruising of the serpent's head would be fulfilled, as God had promised. But unfortunately Cain turned away from God and killed his brother Abel and walked in the way of evil, so God gave Eve a son whom she named Seth, and its meaning is substitute or appointed, that is, he was a substitute for Cain, who turned away, and for righteous Abel, who died. Appointed, that is, God appointed him to be the head of the blessed offspring.

4.22.0.en: Seth lived with God, then begot a son whom he named Enos, and its meaning is man, and he lived like his father with God, praying and offering animal sacrifices, that is, burnt offerings, to please God, and by this the blessed offspring began to increase, and he took care to mention the name of God and to live with Him.

4.22.1.en: If you have lost something, whether of the material things of this world or the spiritual things, by your falling into sin, be confident that your merciful God, if you return to Him, is ready to compensate you for all you have lost, that you may thank Him and return to your strong spiritual life and enjoy fellowship with Him.

5.0.0.en: Methuselah: he is the man who lived longest on the earth, reaching the age of 969 years, but his life also ended in death, so what matters is not the length or shortness of life but life with God, as was testified of Enoch (v. 27).

5.1.0.en: Noah is the tenth from Adam, and the meaning of his name is rest or repose, and perhaps what is meant by the name is the rest that man enjoys after the Flood, evident in God's care and promises, in addition to Noah's rest throughout his life, since he found grace in the eyes of God. The Book mentions Noah's three sons, "Shem, Ham and Japheth", who became the heads of the tribes that were formed after the Flood and populated the earth.

5.1.1.en: You can find grace in the eyes of God like Noah if you hold fast to your faith however much those around you cast doubt on you, and you are also able, if you keep His commandments and try to apply them in your life, to feel His presence with you and to be distinguished by an inexpressible joy and happiness and to be saved from all dangers.

5.1.2.en: The life of Adam can be summarized as follows:

5.1.3.en: 1- The creation of Adam from the dust and the breath of God (ch. 2:7).

5.1.4.en: 2- God's commandment to him in the garden not to eat of the tree of the knowledge of good and evil (ch. 2:16, 17).

5.1.5.en: 3- Adam names the animals by their names and works in the garden (ch. 2:19).

5.1.6.en: 4- God creates Eve from Adam's side (ch. 2:21).

5.1.7.en: 5- The fall of Adam and Eve (ch. 3).

5.1.8.en: 6- The expulsion of Adam and Eve from the garden (ch. 3:24).

5.1.9.en: 7- The begetting of Cain and Abel and Cain's killing of Abel (ch. 4).

5.1.11.en: 9- The death of Adam and his descendants (ch. 5). Noah's ark

6.0.s.en: (1) The spread of sin and the punishment of

6.0.0.en: The sons of God: that is, the sons of Seth and Enos, who lived with God and bore His blessed name (ch. 4:26). The daughters of men: they are the descendants of Cain, and they were called so because they lived preoccupied with the flesh and the material concerns that belong to men.

6.0.1.en: People multiplied and increased, and the descendants of Seth lived with God, separated from the descendants of Cain, who were preoccupied with honor and possessions and abandoned the worship of God. The sons of Seth admired the material beauty of the daughters of Cain and married them, so good was mixed with evil and evil prevailed in all the world. Thus the sons of God did not keep their separation from evil; when they became negligent they lost their purity, and everyone was occupied with the desires of the world and departed from God.

6.0.2.en: Let your heart be praying for the whole world, and even seek the souls of all by every means, but beware of mixing with the evil of the wicked in their talk, their gatherings and their evil desires. Hold fast to the commandments of God and reject every evil however small, to please God in all your works.

6.1.0.en: Shall not judge: My Spirit will not continue to reprove the wicked man forever, since He was reproving them through the conscience, but they reject its voice.

6.1.1.en: His straying: his departure from God and his absorption in evil desires.

6.1.2.en: He is flesh: he is a man who inclined to material desires.

6.1.3.en: His days shall be a hundred and twenty years: God gives him a last opportunity to repent, 120 years, which is the time of building the ark.

6.1.4.en: God was grieved by man's increasing evils and his refusal to repent, so He decided to destroy him because he rejected Him, but in His fatherly tenderness He gave him a last opportunity to repent, a long opportunity of 120 years, during which Noah would proclaim the destruction of the wicked if they did not repent.

6.2.0.en: Tyrants: the sons of Cain, who sought honor, position and domination.

6.2.1.en: The giants: the sons born from the intermarriage of the sons of Seth with the daughters of Cain, who lived in evil and in seeking earthly glory and honor, so they had a name on the earth but were rejected by God. Evil and domination were not limited to the sons of Cain but spread in the whole world through the mixing of the sons of Seth with the sons of Cain, so all the offspring became wicked, and they all sought material power and not God.

6.3.0.en: God noticed the spread of evil in the world and people's continuing in this evil every day and their constant refusal to repent, and for this the Holy Spirit portrays for us the extent of God's grief, because man did not fulfill His purpose, which is friendship with Him and walking in the way of righteousness.

6.4.0.en: It repented him: a human expression that literally means "regret..", but what is meant here is a portrayal of the extent of the grief of God's heart.

6.4.1.en: God decided to destroy the wicked because man would not benefit from remaining on the earth but would increase in evil, so a greater punishment awaited him. So out of His mercy and justice He decided to end his life, and at the same time gave him a last opportunity to repent, that perhaps he might return to Him. Also He destroyed the beasts, although they had not sinned, but they were defiled by the evil of man for whose sake they were created; he did not thank God for these animals but on the contrary used them in his desires.

6.4.2.en: Note, beloved, how evil grieves God's heart and how your repentance and return rejoice Him, so be a source of making His heart glad, and do not let the enemy use you to hurt Him, lest you fall under the authority of His discipline.

6.5.s.en: (3) The corruption of the earth and the destruction of man

6.5.0.en: It appears from these verses not only the spread of evil and corruption in the world, but also that every man had done evil and therefore he is responsible for corrupting himself, for God does not take anyone for the fault of another. Noah's boldness with God also appears, as He tells him of the decision to destroy the wicked world, because he was the only one, with his household, who believed in God, and he is the one who would carry the message of repentance for 120 years to the whole world by building the ark before them, that perhaps they would return to God and leave their sins and enter the ark with him.

6.5.1.en: Do not make light of the voice of God that calls you to repentance and to turning back from your sins, whether in the Holy Bible, in the Church or on the tongue of those around you, for God loves you and awaits your return. So offer repentance today and renew your covenant with Him, that you may regain your peace and gladden your heart.

6.6.0.en: Gopher: it is the wood of the cypress or camphor, trees whose wood is durable, does not rot, and whose height is great.

6.6.1.en: Rooms: stories, so the ark was to be of three stories, lower, middle and upper.

6.6.2.en: Pitch: it is the asphalt that is formed from petroleum residues.

6.6.3.en: God commanded Noah to make the ark, which is a large ship covered from above, and the ark consists of three stories that he makes from the durable gopher wood that does not rot, then he is to pitch it within and without with pitch to prevent water from seeping through the wood. The pitch signifies the importance of man's protecting himself from the entry of the thoughts of the world into him, so that he may enjoy the purity that appears outwardly in his conduct and inwardly in his thoughts and the intentions of his heart.

6.7.0.en: The dimensions of the ark are 300 cubits, that is, 135 meters, because the cubit is the cubit of a man, that is, 45 cm, and the breadth 50 cubits, that is, 22.5 meters, while the height is thirty cubits, that is, 13.5 meters. The length (300) is the product of (100 x 3), and the number 100 signifies the people of God, as He said in the parable of the lost sheep (a hundred sheep), while the three signifies the Holy Trinity, and the meaning is the people of God who believe in Him.

6.7.1.en: As for the breadth of fifty, it is like the fiftieth Jubilee year in which slaves are set free and those sentenced to death for having killed someone by mistake, and the day of Pentecost (the fiftieth) is also the day on which the Holy Spirit descended, so the number (50) signifies the forgiveness and love of God. As for the height, it is (30), like the elevation of Joseph to the throne of Egypt at the age of thirty, and the meaning is elevation to God, that is, hope in Him, and therefore the meaning of the dimensions is faith, love and hope.

6.8.0.en: He commanded him to make windows for the ark, which are to be in the upper story, since the ark has three stories, and they are to be a cubit from the roof of the ark. They are for seeing the heaven and the rains through them, and they signify man's looking to heaven, that is, being spiritual.

6.8.1.en: As for the door, it is to be in the side of the ark for man and animals to enter through it, and being in the side of the ark it signifies the pierced side of Christ, through which we find our salvation and redemption.

6.9.0.en: He declares the purpose of building the ark, which is to protect man and animals from perishing in the Flood that comes upon the world because of its evil, and everyone who believes in God enters the ark and is saved from destruction. Therefore the churches are built in the form of an ark, because in them we find our salvation, and there is no salvation outside the Church.

6.10.0.en: God's covenant with Noah is that He would keep him from destruction because of his faith. For a covenant is always between two parties, each fulfilling his duties: man's duty is faith and life with God, and God's responsibility is to keep man from destruction and give him life and happiness with Him.

6.10.1.en: Would that you enjoy covenants with God, for He is ready to give you His infinite love and keep you in all your ways if you remain faithful in carrying out your covenants, and if you fall short, He is long-suffering, so return to Him quickly.

6.11.0.en: He also commanded him to take two of every animal, that is, a male and a female of all animals of their different kinds, whether beasts, creeping things or birds ... etc., so that offspring might remain for them.

6.12.0.en: God also cared for the food of Noah and the animals, so He commanded him to gather of the plants enough for him and all who were with him, and Noah obeyed all God's commands.
